The absolute eosinophil counts in the blood of patients with neoplasms are significantly higher than in the blood of control subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the absolute number of eosinophils as an aid to diagnosis in cases where a necrotic lesion of unknown origin was present.
the use of absolute eosinophil counts as a screening test to detect neoplastic diseases.
the study of the role of eosinophils in neoplasia and the use of the absolute number of eosinophila in diagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a low absolute eosinophilic count (AEC) is a risk factor for the development of acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
a normal absolute eosinophilic count does not exclude the diagnosis of Hodgkin’s disease, but an elevated absolute count is highly suggestive of this diagnosis.

the absolute eosinophilia in neoplasms is not due to a specific eosinophil-stimulating factor, but to an increase in the number of circulating eosinophils, which is due to a decrease in the number of eosinophils in the tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the use of the absolute number of eosinophils as an index of the activity of neoplastic disease is not a reliable index.
we found a positive correlation between the absolute eosinophils counts and the severity of the COVID-19 disease, but not with the mortality.
the absolute eosinophils count is not a good marker to predict the presence or absence of cancer in patients with a history of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the absolute eosinophilia count is a useful tool for the diagnosis of parasitic infections, especially in patients with eosinophilia and no obvious cause, and it can also be used as a tool for the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with helminthic infections.
the absolute eosinophilia count can be used as a biomarker of disease severity in COVID-19.
eosinophils are important for the control of the parasite infection, but not the disease.
